name: Retatrutide
used_for: Investigated in clinical trials (sponsored by Eli Lilly) for weight reduction in adults with obesity or overweight, type 2 diabetes, knee osteoarthritis and other obesity-related conditions. It is also promoted online as a weight-loss compound, including as unregulated 'research' product.

entries.text: In a 48-week phase 2 trial, once-weekly subcutaneous injections were studied at maintenance doses of 1 mg, 4 mg, 8 mg and 12 mg, with different starting doses (2 mg or 4 mg) for some groups; gastrointestinal side effects were more frequent at higher starting doses.
entries.population: Adults with obesity or overweight (338 enrolled), under clinical trial supervision

entries.text: In a 24-week phase 2 trial, once-weekly subcutaneous doses with maintenance levels from 0.5 mg to 12 mg were studied and compared with placebo and dulaglutide.
entries.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes (281 randomised), under clinical trial supervision

entries.text: In a 40-week phase 3 trial, once-weekly subcutaneous doses of 4 mg, 9 mg and 12 mg were studied versus placebo.
entries.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes not controlled by diet and exercise alone (537 randomised)

entries.text: In an 80-week phase 3 trial, once-weekly subcutaneous doses of 4 mg, 9 mg and 12 mg were studied versus placebo.
entries.population: Adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes (1152 randomised)

administration_guidance.text: In the phase 3 TRIUMPH-2 trial, retatrutide was given as self-administered once-weekly subcutaneous injections. Retatrutide is investigational, so no label guidance on timing, meals, or storage exists.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: An educational peptide site says the time of day is flexible given the drug's long half-life, that morning injection lets side effects be noticed while awake and evening injection lets nausea fall during sleep, that food does not affect absorption of a subcutaneous injection, and that high-fat meals on injection days are best avoided. It also says reconstituted vials are kept upright in the refrigerator. These are the site's statements, not label guidance, since retatrutide is unapproved.
administration_guidance.label: internet

side_effects.text: In the phase 2 obesity trial, the most common adverse events were gastrointestinal, were dose-related, mostly mild to moderate, and were partly reduced by a lower starting dose. Dose-dependent increases in heart rate peaked at 24 weeks and declined afterward.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: In TRIUMPH-2 (type 2 diabetes and obesity), diarrhea occurred in 27 to 34% of retatrutide recipients vs 13% with placebo and nausea in 14 to 28% vs 8%.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: In TRIUMPH-2, dysesthesia occurred in 4 to 7% of retatrutide recipients vs 1% with placebo and hypotension in 1 to 6% vs under 1%. Permanent discontinuation due to adverse events or death was 8% to 12% across the retatrutide groups, vs 5% with placebo.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: In TRANSCEND-T2D-1 (40 weeks), the most frequent adverse events were mostly mild to moderate gastrointestinal events that subsided over time. Discontinuations due to adverse events were 2 to 5% with retatrutide and 0% with placebo, and no severe hypoglycemia was reported.
side_effects.label: research

internet_claims.claim: A video reviewer describes quitting retatrutide after six months and reports muscle loss and side effects alongside weight loss (based on the video title and description).
A video presents a list of benefits of retatrutide beyond weight loss, citing what people using it report (based on the video title and description).
A video discusses 'microdosing' retatrutide and GLP-1 drugs alongside other peptides in a Q&A; the description carries a promotional discount code for a peptide vendor.

Futurism reports that people using black-market retatrutide describe dramatic weight loss (some over 70 pounds), while some describe painful skin sensations, and experts warn about unknown contents and contamination.

A dietitian's blog says retatrutide is still experimental and unapproved, that early trials suggest up to about 24% weight loss, that its safety is not yet established, and warns against buying 'research chemical' versions online.

research.summary: Phase 2, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial (NEJM) of once-weekly subcutaneous retatrutide for 48 weeks in 338 adults with obesity or overweight. Funded by Eli Lilly.
research.finding: Average body weight fell by about 24% at 48 weeks with the 12 mg dose versus about 2% with placebo. Side effects were mostly gastrointestinal and dose-related; heart rate increased in a dose-dependent way.

research.summary: Phase 2 randomized, double-blind trial (Lancet) of retatrutide in 281 US adults with type 2 diabetes, compared with placebo and dulaglutide over 24 weeks.
research.finding: Higher retatrutide doses lowered HbA1c by roughly 2 percentage points at 24 weeks, more than placebo and, at higher doses, more than dulaglutide.

research.summary: Phase 3 TRANSCEND-T2D-1 trial (Lancet, 2026), 40 weeks, 537 adults with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled by diet and exercise.
research.finding: HbA1c and body weight fell more with retatrutide than placebo at all three doses; side effects were mostly mild to moderate gastrointestinal events.

research.summary: Phase 3 TRIUMPH-2 trial (Lancet, published online 29 Sep 2026), 80 weeks, 1152 adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes.
research.finding: Body weight fell by about 12% (4 mg), 17% (9 mg) and 19% (12 mg) versus about 5% with placebo; gastrointestinal adverse events were the most frequent.

research.summary: Completed phase 3 trial (Eli Lilly) of once-weekly retatrutide in adults with obesity or overweight and knee osteoarthritis. The registry record listed no posted results when checked.
research.finding: The registry confirms this phase 3 program exists; no results were verified from this record.

research.summary: ClinicalTrials.gov expanded access record from Eli Lilly for single-patient pre-approval access to retatrutide, described as investigational, for adults with severe obesity and serious complications who cannot join a trial.
research.finding: Confirms retatrutide is described by its sponsor as investigational and available outside trials only through a restricted expanded access route.

dose.summary: Not approved. Phase 3 trials used 4, 9 or 12 mg weekly after starting at 2 mg and stepping up every 4 weeks. Online users describe starting at 1 or 2 mg; research-grade products are unregulated.

mechanism.summary: Acts on three hormone receptors (GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon), lowering appetite and possibly raising energy use.

items.text: Retatrutide is a single peptide that activates the GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon receptors.
items.label: research

best_documented_effect.summary: About 24% average weight loss at 48 weeks on 12 mg in a phase 2 trial, and about 19% at 80 weeks in people with obesity and type 2 diabetes.
